title.rendered: Ask, Seek, Knock: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: Ask, and it will be given to you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened to you. Three verbs. Three promises. One Father who delights to answer the child who dares to come.

content.rendered:
Ask, and it will be given to you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened to you. Three verbs. Three promises. One Father who delights to answer the child who dares to come.

The Gospel For Today | Monday, July 27, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives, and he who seeks finds, and to him who knocks it will be opened.”
Matthew 7:7-8 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Jesus places these two verses at the very heart of the Sermon on the Mount, the greatest teaching on Kingdom life ever delivered. He has already unfolded the beatitudes, the character of the Kingdom, the ethics of the disciples, the way to pray, the treasure that lasts, the freedom from anxiety. Now He turns and simply says, “Ask.” The whole life of authority in the Kingdom is built on the readiness of the King’s children to come and ask their Father for what they need.

The Greek verbs Jesus uses are in the present continuous imperative, meaning the action is ongoing, not one-off. The Amplified Bible Classic Edition captures the sense of it beautifully: “Keep on asking and it will be given you; keep on seeking and you will find; keep on knocking [reverently] and [the door] will be opened to you” (Matthew 7:7 AMPC). And The Passion Translation renders it: “Ask, and the gift is yours. Seek, and you’ll discover. Knock, and the door will be opened for you” (Matthew 7:7 TPT). This is not a formula the believer manipulates. This is a posture the believer walks in.

Notice the three levels of engagement. Asking is verbal. Seeking is active pursuit. Knocking is persistence at a specific door. The progression teaches how spiritual authority in prayer actually works. First, you speak. Then, you move. Then, when you know where the answer lies, you keep on standing at the door until it opens. This is not begging. This is the confident engagement of a child who knows the Father is willing to answer.

And notice the universal scope of the promise. “For everyone who asks receives.” Not most. Not those with the right technique. Not the specially anointed. Everyone. The invitation is open to every believer walking with the King. This is what makes the sentence so revolutionary in the context of first-century Judaism. Jesus was not describing a rare experience reserved for prophets and priests. He was describing the ordinary access of every child of the Father.

For Gospelbuzz readers stepping into a new month of walking in the believer’s authority, the invitation is exactly what it has always been. Come. Ask. Seek. Knock. The Father who watches over you delights in the children who come confidently. There is nothing you carry today that He is unwilling to hear. There is no request you can raise in the name of Jesus that He will dismiss. Walk in the ask today. Walk in the seek today. Walk in the knock today. The door is opening.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that You have invited me to ask, to seek, to knock. This is not begging. This is the confident engagement of a child who knows the Father is willing to answer. I come today with the requests on my heart. I speak them plainly in the name of Jesus. I pursue what You have promised. I stand at the door of the answer with settled persistence. Every believer who asks receives. I am one of those who ask. I walk in that promise today, confident that You hear me. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

The Father has invited me to ask, seek, and knock. Every believer who asks receives. I come today with confidence, not begging but engaging. The door is opening.

  • Luke 11:5-13 (NKJV): The friend at midnight and the persistence Jesus commends
  • Jeremiah 33:3 (NKJV): Call to Me, and I will answer you
